html:
The Ngameni are an Aboriginal Australian people of the far northeast of South Australia, on the lower Diamantina River and around Goyder Lagoon. Their language is no longer spoken.

Their neighbours were the Karangura, Yarluyandi, Wangkangurru and Diyari. Lutheran missionaries opened a mission on Cooper Creek among the Diyari in 1866, and many people of the region came into its orbit. The stock route later called the Birdsville Track crossed this country.
